bib.title: Large Language Models Understand and Can Be Enhanced by Emotional Stimuli

question: Can LLMs understand emotional stimuli, and does appending emotional phrases to a prompt (EmotionPrompt) improve their task performance?
hypothesis: Psychology shows emotional stimuli (expectancy, confidence, social influence) help people, so appending such phrases should improve LLM performance.
contributions: We propose EmotionPrompt to thoroughly study the emotional intelligence of large language models.
Extensive experiments on deterministic and generative tasks, with standard and human evaluation.
In-depth analysis of the rationales behind EmotionPrompt.

method.summary: Eleven fixed emotional sentences (EP01-EP11, designed from three psychological theories) are appended to the original prompt. Effect is measured on 24 Instruction Induction tasks and 21 BIG-Bench tasks across six LLMs (zero-shot, 5-shot), on TruthfulQA with three models, and in a 106-participant human study of GPT-4 outputs on 30 questions.
method.task: prompt augmentation for QA, instruction induction, BIG-Bench reasoning, open-ended generation

datasets.name: Instruction Induction
datasets.size: 24 tasks; 100 samples per task for most, 25 (Cause Selection), 16 (Common Concept), 15 (Formality)

datasets.name: BIG-Bench Instruction Induction (BBII) subset
datasets.source: Srivastava et al. / Zhou et al. [39]

inference.temperature: 0.7 for ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Llama 2; remaining LLMs at default settings; temperature sweep 0.0/0.4/0.7/1.0/1.5 on 8 Instruction Induction tasks
inference.samples: inferred: one run per prompt-model-task (no repeats, seeds or variance reported); at temperature 0.7 this leaves sampling noise unquantified
inference.prompting: Zero-shot: original prompt + one emotional stimulus appended. Few-shot (Instruction Induction only): same prompts plus 5 randomly sampled input-output pairs appended, template 'prompt/EmotionPrompt + demonstration'. BIG-Bench zero-shot only.

parameters.prompt_sources: human-designed original prompts, and APE-generated prompts [39] with stimulus added
parameters.Ours(avg): per-stimulus task-average, then mean over the 11 stimuli
parameters.Ours(max): per task, the best of the 11 stimuli, then mean over tasks

other.attention_analysis: Flan-T5-Large, gradient-norm input attention contribution of each word on a Sentiment Analysis task, averaged over test samples (method of [40])
other.human_study: 106 participants rate two GPT-4 answers (vanilla vs EmotionPrompt) per question, 1-5 on performance, truthfulness, responsibility; Relative Gain = Metric_EmotionPrompt - Metric_vanilla; no statistical test described
other.stimulus_selection: inferred: no dev/test split is mentioned, so the 'max' stimulus is chosen on the same evaluation data

metrics.name: BIG-Bench normalized preferred metric
metrics.definition: defined in [30]; 100 = human experts, 0 = random guessing, can be below 0

metrics.name: TruthfulQA % true / % info
metrics.definition: scored by fine-tuned GPT-judge and GPT-info

metrics.name: Human ratings
metrics.definition: 1-5 scale on performance, truthfulness, responsibility, averaged over 106 raters

eval.protocol: Results averaged over tasks per model; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported for automatic evaluation. Human study reports means and SDs; paper notes high variance due to subjectivity.

evidence.quote: For ChatGPT, we utilize gpt-3.5-turbo (0613) and set temperature parameter to 0.7. For GPT-4 and Llama 2, we set the temperature to 0.7. The remaining LLMs are evaluated using their default settings.

results.claim: Headline: relative improvement of EmotionPrompt over the original prompt on Instruction Induction.
results.setup: 24 Instruction Induction tasks, six models (Flan-T5-Large, Vicuna, Llama 2, BLOOM, ChatGPT, GPT-4), mean over models and tasks; the paper does not state which Table 1 row or averaging the 8.00% comes from
results.quote: an relative improvement of 8.00% in Instruction Induction and 115% in BIG-Bench
results.note: Derivation unstated. Recomputing from Table 1 Ours(max) vs Original over the four Instruction Induction settings (zero/few-shot x human/APE prompts) gives 6.95, 7.38, 9.23, 8.44 percent, mean about 8.0, so the headline appears to use the per-task best-of-11 (max) row, not the avg row.

results.claim: Headline: relative improvement on BIG-Bench.
results.setup: 21 BIG-Bench tasks, zero-shot, six models; derivation not stated
results.quote: an relative improvement of 8.00% in Instruction Induction and 115% in BIG-Bench
results.note: Not reproducible from Table 1 with a single obvious pair: Ours(avg) vs Original with APE prompts is 2.39 -> 5.20 (+117%); human-designed Original 10.16 -> Ours(max) 11.92 is +17%; APE 2.39 -> Ours(max) 7.47 is +213%.

results.claim: Instruction Induction zero-shot, human-designed prompts: Original mean accuracy.
results.setup: 24 Instruction Induction tasks, six models (Flan-T5-Large, Vicuna, Llama 2, BLOOM, ChatGPT, GPT-4), mean over models and tasks, zero-shot, human-designed prompts, Original row
results.table: Table 1, row Original (Instruction Induction +Zero-shot), column Average

results.setup: 24 Instruction Induction tasks, six models (Flan-T5-Large, Vicuna, Llama 2, BLOOM, ChatGPT, GPT-4), mean over models and tasks, zero-shot, human-designed prompts; mean over 11 stimuli

results.setup: Instruction Induction, avg over 6 models; zero-shot 0.33 vs few-shot 2.05
results.quote: the improvement brought by EmotionPrompt is larger in few-shot setting than zero-shot settings (0.33 vs. 2.05, in terms of average improvement)

results.setup: 21 BIG-Bench tasks, zero-shot, APE-generated prompts, mean of six models

results.claim: Human study: average improvement across performance, truthfulness and responsibility.
results.setup: 106 participants rating GPT-4 answers to 30 questions, vanilla vs EmotionPrompt, 1-5 scales
results.quote: (10.9% average improvement in terms of performance, truthfulness, and responsibility metrics)
results.note: Abstract only; Sec 2.3.3 reports Fig 5/6 (plots), no table of means and no significance test. Footnote 3 concedes high variance.

results.claim: TruthfulQA: average improvement in truthfulness and informativeness.
results.setup: TruthfulQA 817 questions, ChatGPT, Vicuna-13b, Flan-T5-Large; 'best result of EmotionPrompt' used in Fig 7
results.quote: average improvement of 19% and 12% in terms of truthfulness and informativeness scores
results.note: The 19%/12% are for the best stimulus (Fig 7 caption); per-stimulus Table 3 varies widely.

results.claim: TruthfulQA Vicuna-13b: EP01 collapses % true.
results.setup: Vicuna-13b, TruthfulQA, EP01
results.note: Table 3 also shows Vicuna %info at 0.00 for EP02-EP08 and CoT, i.e. near-zero informativeness (likely refusals or non-answers) with %true near 1.0.

results.claim: TruthfulQA ChatGPT: EP01 raises %info but lowers %true.
results.setup: ChatGPT, TruthfulQA, EP01

results.claim: Relative Gain (zero-shot Instruction Induction, human prompts) rises with model size; Vicuna highest, Flan-T5-Large lowest.
results.setup: Vicuna 13B; Llama 2 13B 6.00, ChatGPT 4.32, GPT-4 0.85, BLOOM 0.51, Flan-T5-Large 0.28
results.table: Table 6, row Vicuna, column Relative Gain
results.note: Table 6 does not show monotonic increase with size: BLOOM (176B) is 0.51 and Vicuna 13B is top.

results.claim: Larger temperature widens EmotionPrompt gain; EmotionPrompt less sensitive to temperature.
results.setup: 8 Instruction Induction tasks, 5 temperatures, 6 LLMs (Vicuna and Llama 2 lack temperature 0.0)
results.note: Read from Fig 11 only; no numbers in text.

results.claim: Best stimulus differs by benchmark: EP02 best on Instruction Induction, EP06 best on BIG-Bench; EP02 does poorly on BIG-Bench.
results.setup: stimulus ranking averaged over 6 LLMs, human and APE prompts
results.note: Figs 9-10 are plots; text says EP02 'surpasses the worst one at 6.06%' in the Introduction.

results.claim: Combining stimuli: more stimuli generally better but little or no benefit when a single stimulus is already good.
results.setup: ChatGPT, 7 tasks (SA, SS, WC, CS, LA, Sum, SW), Table 5

results.claim: Attention analysis: positive words contribute over 50% on 4 of 8 tasks.
results.setup: Flan-T5-Large, gradient-norm attribution
results.note: Read from Fig 8; text: 'the contributions of positive words pass 50% on 4 tasks, even approach 70% on 2 tasks'.

results.claim: Two failure cases of EmotionPrompt in the human study (more definitive wording; shorter summary).
results.setup: Tables 19-20, GPT-4

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests for the automatic evaluations; temperature 0.7 for three models.
'max' headline picks the best of 11 stimuli per task; no separate selection set is described.
No control with neutral filler text of equal length, so the effect of emotional content versus extra tokens is untested.
BIG-Bench evaluated zero-shot only 'due to constrained computation devices'; GPT-4 not evaluated on TruthfulQA 'due to constrained budget'.
Human study: 106 raters, 90% students aged 20-25, one GPT-4 answer per condition per question, high variance conceded (footnote 3).
Authors concede the finding 'conflicts with existing studies on human emotional intelligence' and the mechanism is unclear.
Models are 2023 snapshots (gpt-3.5-turbo 0613); stimuli effects may not transfer to later models (inferred).
